Bounded multi-year ice body: mass store, SIA flux on a short flowline, declared erosion proxy.

What this module is
-------------------
A **finite, bounded** ice-mass model on a short one-dimensional flowline of native 30 m cells:

* ice thickness is the state; the ice **surface is recomputed every step** as ``bed + thickness``
  (there is no independent surface field that could disagree with the ice);
* flow is the shallow-ice approximation (SIA) for **deformation (creep) only**. It is *not* basal
  sliding: no sliding law is implemented here, and nothing is called "sliding velocity";
* mass is conserved in three separate accounts: ice volume, liquid water, and — separately —
  rock removed from a **finite, explicitly supplied** bedrock stock;
* a declared erosion proxy produces a derived ``bed_delta_m``. It is returned, never written back
  into any TD bed, and it is not presented as a coupled bed-feedback result.

The SIA flux, with units
------------------------
For a flowline along ``x`` with fixed width ``W``, thickness ``H`` and surface ``s = bed + H``:

    q(face) = W * (2A / (n + 2)) * (rho g)^n * H_f^(n + 2) * |ds/dx|^(n - 1) * (-ds/dx)

with

===========  ========================================  ==================================
symbol       meaning                                   unit
===========  ========================================  ==================================
``A``        creep parameter (Glen flow law)           Pa^-n s^-1
``n``        Glen exponent                             dimensionless (3 here)
``rho``      ice density                               kg m^-3
``g``        gravitational acceleration                m s^-2
``H_f``      mean of the two adjacent thicknesses     m
``ds/dx``    surface slope between the two cells       dimensionless (m m^-1)
``W``        cell width (flowline width)               m
``q``        volume flux through that face            m^3 s^-1
===========  ========================================  ==================================

``A`` is **not** a dimensionless fudge factor. ``A = 2.4e-24 Pa^-3 s^-1`` is the declared
typical Glen ``n = 3`` value; if a caller wants a lumped coefficient instead, it must say so and
carry its own dimensions, because ``(2A/(n+2)) * (rho g)^n`` is what is actually multiplied.
This module only accepts the dimensional ``A`` above.

Stability is explicit and declared
----------------------------------
The face diffusivity is ``D = (2A/(n+2)) (rho g)^n H_f^(n+2) |ds/dx|^(n-1)`` (m^2 s^-1), and the
step is bounded by ``dt <= CFL * dx^2 / D_max`` with ``CFL = 0.25``. An interval longer than
``MAX_SUBSTEPS * dt_limit`` is **refused** — the caller must refine, not ask this module to take an
unstable step. Within the limit the step is split into an integer number of fixed sub-steps, and
per-cell outgoing flux is clipped by the available volume (``min(flux, available)``) so thickness
can never go negative. Clipping is recorded, never silently applied as "flux = 0".

What is deliberately not here
-----------------------------
No basal sliding, no ice temperature, no three-dimensional state, no calving, no glacier-lake
outburst, no real-world glacier prediction, and no verdict that a given snow patch *is* a glacier.
A multi-year net loss or gain in this store says nothing about whether a glacier exists.

G8 bounded basin ocean core: conservative water and heat transport.

Scope, stated first
-------------------
This is a **finite, explicitly bounded ocean basin**: a declared connected wet mask, a
declared depth per cell, and explicit boundary faces. It is **not** a global ocean, not
a general circulation model, and not a momentum/Navier-Stokes solver.

What it deliberately is *not*
-----------------------------
* **No random warm/cold current labels.** Flow comes from a declared wind bearing and
  speed acting on real per-cell depth; the resulting face fluxes are non-zero, bounded,
  and auditable.
* **No salinity.** No salt state is built here, so no salt budget is claimed. A later
  card that adds salt must add its own conservative account; this one never implies it.
* **No diffusion dressed up as circulation.** Heat moves only with the conservative
  face advection below. Spreading sea-surface temperature by a diffusion operator and
  calling it a current is exactly what this module refuses to do.

Water account
-------------
Every cell holds a volume in m³. A shared internal face carries **one** per-step
transported **volume in m³** that is applied with opposite signs to its two
neighbours, so the face bookkeeping itself cannot create or destroy water.

Note the distinction the field names keep: the quantity is **volume moved during the
step**, not a rate. It is `speed·dt/dx · V_upwind`, so `dt` is already inside it. A
caller must not multiply by `dt` a second time; anyone wanting a discharge in m³/s must
divide by `dt` explicitly.

An open boundary face discharges out of the **geometric domain edge** and is booked as
outflow. A land coast is **never** used as an open drain: only a face that leaves the
declared grid can be `open`, and a wet cell bordering land is either `closed` or has no
exit at all.

Heat account
------------
Heat moves with the water, on the **upwind** value, and is never re-diffused:

    Δ(V·T)_cell = Σ(inflow·T_upwind) − Σ(outflow·T_cell)

The transported quantity is therefore `m³·°C` — a **relative heat content** under a
constant specific heat, with the reference at 0 °C. It is *not* an absolute energy in
joules. Reporting joules requires multiplying by an explicit `ρ·c_p`:

    energy_J = (V·T)[m³·°C] · ρ·c_p [J/(m³·°C)]

and even then the value is referenced to 0 °C. `SEAWATER_VOLUMETRIC_HEAT_CAPACITY_J_M3K`
is declared so that conversion is possible; the ledger below never claims to be in
joules.

Negative temperatures are legitimate (the reference is 0 °C), so the heat scale used for
the tolerance is `Σ|V·T|`, not `|Σ V·T|`: a basin straddling 0 °C must not get an
artificially tiny tolerance just because its signed total happens to cancel.

Shore and land
--------------
A land cell is never transported through: an internal face requires **both** cells wet.
Two wet basins separated by land therefore stay separate, and neither can drain into the
other around a shore.

CFL
---
The speed is a **prescribed current speed derived from a declared wind proxy**, not a
solved wind stress or momentum balance. The scheme requires
`wind_speed_m_s · dt_s / dx ≤ 1`, refused otherwise rather than silently reduced.

G4 limited vapour transport: explicit finite volume on a constant axial wind.

Scope (stated before anything else)
-----------------------------------
This is a **bounded, single-domain, constant-axial-wind** explicit finite-volume
vapour transport. It is **not** a global atmospheric model, not a continuous wind
or pressure field, and not a GCM. Its whole purpose is to supply the one thing the
existing per-point orographic multiplier lacks: a **mass constraint** on water.

Everything here works in **mass**.
-----------------------------------
Every state is a per-cell mass in **kg**. Time-edge records are `state[edge]`.
Nothing inside the solver is a depth or a density; depth conversion exists only in
`depth_mm()` for reporting.

Three unit facts that are easy to get wrong, and are therefore stated as code:

* a face flux `F` is `kg/(m·s)`, so entering the ledger multiplies it by that
  face's length **and** by `dt` to become kg. For internal faces the length is
  `dx`, and `F = u·V/dx` follows from `F = u·(V/A_cell)·L_face` with
  `A_cell = dx²`, `L_face = dx`;
* `P`, `R` and `E` are **kg per interval** once they reach the update, so any rate
  form must be multiplied by `dt` first;
* an ET given as `m³/interval` converts to **`kg = m³ × ρ`** — multiply by density
  only. Dividing by area would produce `kg/m²`, which is a different quantity from
  a per-cell kg mass. Area appears only when reporting a depth.

`wind_unit` is a **direction** (dimensionless, one of `{0, ±1}` axial pairs), never
a speed. The speed is the explicit `wind_speed_m_s` parameter, and the CFL number
uses the speed: `wind_speed_m_s·dt/dx <= 1`, refused otherwise rather than reduced
silently.

Update order is fixed and each step happens exactly once
--------------------------------------------------------
From `V_old` to `V_new`, per step:

1. **face transport** — fluxes computed from `V_old` only, yielding
   `V_after_transport`. A shared internal face carries **one** flux value that is
   applied with opposite signs to its two neighbours, so nothing is created or
   destroyed by the face bookkeeping itself;
2. **external recycling** — `V_after_recycle = V_after_transport + R` (`R` already
   kg per interval);
3. **condensation** — `P = clip(k·max(gradient,0)·V_after_recycle·dt, 0,
   V_after_recycle)`: precipitation can never exceed the vapour actually present.
   This is the only depletion constraint, and background condensation is drawn from
   `V` as well, never added as a new source;
4. **new state** — `V_new = V_after_recycle − P`.

Transporting twice in one step (advect, then advect "the remainder" again) or
precipitating the same mass twice are both refused by construction: step 1 reads
only `V_old` and later steps read only their own predecessor.

Time is a DAG; a recirculating wind field is legitimate
-------------------------------------------------------
An explicit scheme advances from the previous time edge, so a **closed circulation
in the wind field is perfectly supportable** and is not an error. What is an error
is a *synchronous* dependency cycle — two cells demanding each other's value at the
same instant. That is a topology defect inside one time layer and it raises.

Boundary honesty
----------------
An undeclared inflow is **never** silently zero. The only legitimate zeros are an
explicit `0.` from the caller (`explicit_zero`) and a declared `closed` wall
(`closed_no_flux`). An `unknown_boundary` face produces **no certified zero flux**
and marks the whole result as not certified. Missing sources stay `pending`.

Actual soil-thickness and land-cover consumer for G6 (bounded, one entry point).

What this module is
-------------------
A **consumer**, not a new physics model. It takes four already-produced inputs, each
with its own identity and its own declared status, and derives three separated
outputs:

    inputs                     outputs
    ------                     -------
    parent material (G9/S3)    soil thickness (bulk, m)
    rock physical properties    soil water capacity (mm) and the actual
      (porosity, hardness,       G5 water state it is compared against
       solubility, ...)         suitability (temperature + water + material)
    actual G5 water state       land cover (the actual surface class)
    G3 monthly temperature and
      annual precipitation

Nothing here measures soil. Every number is either an input passed through, a
declared conversion, or a declared engineering ranking.

The three products are deliberately **not** collapsed into one label:

* ``soil`` — thickness and capacity, derived from material and pore space;
* ``suitability`` — how favourable the site is, from temperature, water and
  material, in normalized units;
* ``land_cover`` — the actual surface class the site carries, which consumes the
  suitability **and** the material **and** the water state, not just the annual
  precipitation rescaled onto a colour.

Thickness is **bulk**, and pore volume is not water
--------------------------------------------------
The parent solid volume delivered by G9 is a **solid** volume. Converted to a soil
layer it must go through the pore space exactly once::

    bulk_thickness_m = solid_m3 / ((1 - porosity) * horizontal_area_m2)

This is **not** ``solid / area``: that would give an equivalent *solid* thickness and
would understate the layer by the pore factor. The same module keeps the distinction
that G9 already draws in its own ``soil_delivery.conversion`` note.

What the layer can hold is a **capacity**, and capacity is not a stock::

    soil_water_capacity_mm = bulk_thickness_m * 1000 * available_water_fraction

where ``available_water_fraction`` is a declared constant (not a measurement). The
actual water content comes from G5 as a ``[3, N]`` bucket state; the two are compared
and reported side by side. A full capacity never means "the soil is wet now".

What this module does NOT do
----------------------------
* no soil-water bucket, no ET, no percolation: G5 owns that and is consumed read-only;
* no vegetation growth, biomass, succession or ecology dynamics — land cover is a
  class, not a plant;
* no weathering rate: G9 owns it and its delivered volumes are taken as declared;
* no world generation, no file IO, no default-world wiring;
* no silent coordinate snapping: a reference point that is not a cell centre must pass
  an explicit accepted offset, mirroring ``geology_properties.reference_points_to_cells``.

Status is always explicit
-------------------------
Every output field carries one of: ``computed``, ``declared``, ``pending`` (a required
input is missing) or ``not_available``. A ``pending`` field is never treated as zero
and a ``declared`` engineering constant is never presented as a measurement.

G3 seasonal air adapter: periodic monthly temperature and its declared calendar.

Role boundary (this module is an **adapter**, not a climate model)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Every physical number here comes from the existing v2 layer
(`terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_climate_refinement.sample_climate_v2`,
itself built on the frozen v1 `metric_noise_forcing.sample_climate`). This module
does **not** re-derive a single climatological formula: no new band rule, no new
lapse rate, no new wind table. It re-packages the v2 result as an explicit
**G3 exchange contract** so that S5 (PET/ET) and later G4/G7 can consume it
without guessing what a field means.

What this module answers
------------------------
* monthly and annual **temperature** on absolute world 30 m reference points;
* the **physical calendar** the months refer to (fixed 365-day year, explicit
  month edges in seconds, physical-time index, never a step counter);
* the **prevailing wind** and the exact rule and parameter identity it came from;
* the freezing month count derived **directly** from `monthly_temperature_c <= 0`
  (not from an inverted per-month elevation threshold, see below);
* optionally the existing snow-line diagnostic, passed through unchanged **and
  with its own elevation semantics stated** (it is not computed from the caller's
  elevation sampler, see "Snow line" below).

What this module explicitly does **not** answer (declared, never implied)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
* **No PET and no actual ET.** Temperature-index PET belongs to S5
  (`hydrology_seasonal.SeasonalConfig`), and `available_water` in A1 is a
  relative proxy, not ET. Copying either here would create a second truth.
* **No snowpack, no glacier, no melt.** A monthly-mean temperature crossing zero
  is a threshold diagnostic; it is not accumulation, not snow-water equivalent and
  not ice.
* **No real latitude** and no real climate class. `latitude_band_norm` is a
  synthetic east-west band coordinate (v2 §3.1); there is no degrees value here
  and no `latitude_deg` key is ever emitted.
* **No diurnal range.** A monthly mean is never a daily maximum or minimum.
* **No moisture budget.** Vapour inventory, boundary supply, depletion and
  recycling are G4 scope in a separate module; nothing here closes a water budget.

Why the freezing count is derived from temperature, not from the snow line
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
`metric_climate_refinement.snow_line` solves, per month, the elevation at which
that month's mean crosses 0 C (`h = -T / lapse_rate`). Those per-month thresholds
are only monotone in elevation if the lapse rate is strictly negative and the
month temperature is above zero at sea level; inverting them into a "how many
frozen months at this point" count is therefore not well defined for every point.
Counting `monthly_temperature_c <= 0` at the queried point needs no inversion and
cannot disagree with the temperature it is derived from. The snow-line diagnostic
is still available, but only as an optional pass-through field.

Snow line: its own elevation semantics, not the caller's
--------------------------------------------------------
`sample_climate_v2` and `snow_line` are two different calls with two different
elevation contracts. `snow_line(seed, x, z, parameters=...)` has **no** elevation
argument at all: it solves the crossing from the zero-elevation monthly means and
the lapse rate. Therefore:

* the returned `snow_line` block is **not** driven by the caller's
  `elevation_sampler` or `elevation_m`, and this module never labels it as
  "DEM-driven" or as sharing the elevation source of `monthly_temperature_c`;
* it is reported under its own key with its own declared source, and
  `snow_line_elevation_semantics` says so verbatim;
* it is never used to derive `freezing_month_count` or any temperature field.

Calendar, annual mean and period integration (three different averages)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
The calendar is the v1 month-day table: a fixed 365-day year, no leap day, no
epoch offset and no timezone; month identity repeats every `year_seconds`.

Three distinct quantities are reported and must not be conflated:

* `annual_mean_temperature_c` — the **unweighted arithmetic mean of the twelve
  monthly means**, which is exactly what v2 reports as `BIO1`. It is *not* a
  day-weighted annual mean; month lengths differ by up to three days, so this
  value can differ from a day-weighted mean by a small but real amount.
* `period_mean_temperature_c` — the interval mean over `time_edges_s` under the
  **month-center piecewise-linear convention** that
  `metric_noise_forcing.interval_mean_rain_mm_h` already uses for rain rates.
  A full-year interval therefore reproduces the `annual_weights`-weighted mean
  (trapezoid over month centers), which is a third, different number.
* the per-month values themselves.

None of the three is renamed into another's slot, and each carries its own
declared source note.

Period integration is bounded and free of large-magnitude cancellation
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The interval is assembled from short, local pieces instead of being computed as
`I(end) - I(start)` for one big antiderivative `I`:

* the tail of the start year, measured from the start's own within-year offset;
* `whole_years * annual_integral` in closed form;
* the head of the end year, measured from zero.

Work is therefore bounded by the *number of points and intervals*, never by the
*physical span*: a request covering thirty thousand years costs the same as one
covering a day. Avoiding the antiderivative difference matters numerically, not
just stylistically — near 1e12 s the two antiderivatives are ~1e12 in size, so
their difference loses roughly 1e-10 relative accuracy, which is far larger than
the tolerance any honest interval mean deserves.

Two guards keep that honest rather than merely fast:

* every segment must make progress (`upper > lower`); if floating point collapses
  the step to zero the call raises instead of spinning;
* an interval whose width is not resolvable at the magnitude of its endpoints
  (fewer than `MIN_INTERVAL_ULPS` units in the last place) is rejected, because
  the interval mean would be cancellation noise rather than a measurement.

Budget honesty
--------------
`MAX_SECONDS` is a **post-stage soft check**, not a hard interrupt: it can only
falsify a call after a stage returns, and it cannot interrupt a kernel that is
already stuck. The real protection is structural — bounded loops, a bounded
point count, and a byte budget checked **before** materialisation. Both facts are
stated in `describe()` so no reviewer can mistake one for the other.

Determinism and identity
------------------------
Identical inputs give identical bits in any window, array shape or call order
(guaranteed by v2's canonical query path); this module adds no cache and no
state.

The composite identity binds the **actual request and the actual output**, not
just the arguments: canonicalised coordinates, query shape, the elevation values
that were really used and their declared source, the twelve monthly temperatures,
the band coordinate, the wind bearing, the annual and period means, the calendar,
the parameters, and the source bytes of every kernel involved **including this
module**. Consequences, each covered by a test:

* a different point set, or the same point count at a different place, changes it;
* changing `elevation_m` (or the values a sampler returns) changes it;
* changing the query shape changes it, even for the same point set;
* a sampler is bound by the **values it returned**, never by its function name —
  two differently-named samplers returning identical heights are correctly the
  same product;
* permuting the request arrays does **not** change it: the arrays are canonically
  sorted by `(x, z)` before hashing, so identity is a property of the point set,
  not of request order. The returned arrays keep the caller's own order.

Finite 1600 km fictional-world overview: three continents, islands, mountains, rivers.

What this module produces
-------------------------
One low-resolution **overview / planning map** of a single finite square world frame:
``extent_km`` on a side, ``grid_size`` cell-centre samples per side, node spacing
``extent_km * 1000 / grid_size`` metres (1024 samples over 1600 km is 1562.5 m).
The land is exactly three continents above a declared area gate plus a set of
small islands; nothing touches the frame border.  Elevation, a continuous
mountain belt and a small set of diagnostic mainstem rivers are exported with a
JSON report that records seeds, parameters, method, limitations and checks.

What this module is *not*
-------------------------
* **Not a Terrain Diffusion product.**  Nothing here calls the TD model, the
  native 30 m pages, ``metric_cross_region`` or any stage-one river chain, and no
  array produced here may be fed to those interfaces as terrain.  The grid is a
  ~1.5 km planning grid, not 30 m; the elevation is an analytic construction.
* **Not a hydraulic result.**  No shallow water, no Manning conveyance, no
  sediment, no evapotranspiration.  The rivers are *diagnostic
  contributing-area paths* (one receiver per node, D8, with the filled working
  surface recorded separately from the exported elevation), so "drainage" here
  means "under D8 on this exported grid", never "measured discharge".  No outlet
  is certified natural.
* **Not a stage-one acceptance.**  Passing this module's own checks says the
  three-continent layout, the ocean border and the acyclic river paths hold on
  *this* overview grid; it says nothing about the 30 m TD chain.

Determinism
-----------
Every random decision is drawn from ``sha256``-derived sub-seeds of one world
seed and a stable purpose name (:func:`derive_subseed`), and the noise is sampled
at absolute metre coordinates from the declared frame origin.  Python's
``hash()``, wall-clock time, system entropy and load order are never used, so the
same request reproduces byte-identical arrays.

Coordinate convention
---------------------
``x`` is east, ``z`` is south, both in metres from the north-west frame corner.
Node ``(i, j)`` (row ``i``, column ``j``) samples the *centre* of its cell:
``x = (j + 0.5) * spacing_m``, ``z = (i + 0.5) * spacing_m``; the cell area is
``spacing_m ** 2``.  A ``grid_size`` of N means N x N cell-centre samples that
cover the frame ``[0, extent_m)`` *by cell edges* -- N cells of ``spacing`` each.
The sample centres themselves only span ``(N - 1) * spacing``.  Both numbers are
reported separately (:meth:`OverviewRequest.grid_contract`) and must never be
used interchangeably.

Elevation is metres above the declared sea-level datum (``SEA_LEVEL_M = 0``);
**negative values are sea floor** and are both allowed and expected.

Scope of this module (G2 first card, deliberately narrow)
---------------------------------------------------------
This is a **composition adapter**. Every physical field is read from an existing
core; nothing here is a new distribution rule:

* rock identity, class, hardness and resistance come from
  :mod:`terrain_pipeline.td_lithology_field`;
* the erodible cover thickness comes from
  :mod:`terrain_pipeline.td_material_field`.

The module adds exactly three things the repository did not have:

1. a **non-empty layer column** (`cover` then `bedrock`) with an explicit status
   per layer, so "no source" is recorded as ``unknown_no_source`` and never as a
   silent zero or a silent half-infinite slab;
2. **declared** inputs for the parts that have no model yet -- bedrock/strata
   thickness, joint geometry, fault geometry, and a per-rock extended property
   table (uniaxial compressive strength, intrinsic permeability). Unsupplied
   values stay ``pending``; nothing is invented for the 18 rocks;
3. an explicit adapter to the existing channel-width law, so a real public
   consumer can be driven on purpose rather than by a hidden default.

What is explicitly NOT here
---------------------------
* no second rock table, no re-derivation of ``bed_hardness``/``bank_hardness``
  (they are read, never recomputed), no porosity-to-permeability inversion;
* no tectonic, plate, subsidence or fault-offset model: a fault declaration is
  geometry only and always reports ``strata_offset_status='unverified'``;
* no regolith or soil inventory and no weathering flux. ``cover_thickness_m`` is
  the erodible material thickness, which is **not** soil depth, **not** regolith
  stock and **not** soil water storage;
* no temperature input at all (this module has no thermal field);
* no default-world wiring, no file IO, no environment-query import.

Coordinate semantics (this is the part that is easy to get wrong)
---------------------------------------------------------------
``td_material_field`` samples **cell centres** ``origin + (index + 0.5) * spacing``,
not grid nodes. A 30 m integer reference point therefore sits half a cell away
from the material sample it would be compared with. This module never snaps:

* :func:`geology_column` samples the material field and the lithology field at
  the *same* cell-centre coordinates, by passing those exact centres to
  ``sample_lithology_points``;
* :func:`reference_points_to_cells` is the only place that maps external
  reference points onto cells, it returns the measured offset, and it refuses
  unless the caller accepts that offset explicitly.

Determinism: absolute world metres only, ``world_seed`` sub-seeds taken from the
lithology core's own derivation, and the material seed passed in by the caller
(no third derivation scheme is invented here).

Declared stratigraphy: parallel dipping horizons and a vertical rock query.

Scope (G2 second card)
--------------------
One thing only: turn a **declared, finite** layer stack into world-anchored
geometry, and answer "which layer and which rock is at this (x, z, elevation)?".

* the stack is given by the caller (rock id, vertical thickness, source);
* horizons are **planes**, all with the same strike and dip, so a horizon is
  `h_k = H_k - tan(dip) * u` with `u` the along-dip horizontal coordinate;
* a fault is a **finite** piecewise-discontinuous offset inside a declared band;
* joints are a world-anchored plane family with a measured distance.

What this is NOT
----------------
* not a tectonic, subsidence or provenance reconstruction;
* no folds, unconformities, lenses or lateral facies change;
* no 2D noise rock copied downward: below the deepest horizon the answer is
  `unknown_no_source`, never the surface rock;
* no weathering, erosion, transport or inventory model;
* no default-world wiring, no file IO, no hashing.

Conventions
-----------
``x`` east, ``z`` south, ``[z, x]``. ``elev`` in metres, positive up.
``strike`` is an azimuth in degrees, north = 0, clockwise toward east, so the
*right-hand* dip direction is ``strike + 90``. All trigonometry converts degrees
to radians explicitly. Layer thickness is **vertical** thickness at the anchor
(field name ``vertical_thickness_m``), not true normal thickness; the two differ
by ``cos(dip)`` and must not be confused when a volume is claimed.

``dip`` must satisfy ``0 <= dip < 90``. At 90 degrees a horizon is a vertical
plane and cannot be written as a single-valued height field, so a vertical layer
is refused instead of approximated.

## The mobile column is at repose, not the landform

The gravity phase is deliberately *not* "relax the whole landform to the angle of
repose".  A 264 m standing rock tower is rock: it cannot be at repose and must not be
flattened into one.  The native morphodynamics code already carries the right
semantics -- ``metric_fluvial_morphodynamics.py:584`` keeps ``mobile_base`` as the
running minimum of the bed -- so the mobile column here is only the material that has
actually been detached and is still in transit.  Untouched rock has an empty mobile
column, and the relaxation provably leaves it alone (``available = bed - mobile_base
== 0``).

That distinction was measured, not assumed.  Throwaway probes gave every cell of the
tower a loose skin and relaxed it: 1.8e7 m3 of internal relocation against 5.2e3 m3
of detachment, eating the volcanic plug column down by 36.5 m and *raising* karst
cells by 104 m.  The in-transit column relocated 3.9e5 m3 on the same chart and held
the maximum column loss to the incision depth, 8.6 m.  So the detachment term is
bounded by a declared rock *floor*, not by the mobile column -- otherwise no material
could ever be loosened in the first place.

## Structural guarantees

* the perimeter stays at zero displacement and zero change, because both new fields
  are tapered to zero wherever the parent displacement is zero and every operator runs
  inside a sacrificial outer ring;
* ``floor <= bed`` and ``mobile_base <= bed`` everywhere, because both are clamped to
  the bed after every phase;
* no cell is ever cut below its rock floor, so nothing is silently clipped.

The rock floor is a declared depth below the *roughened* surface -- the surface the
river actually flows on -- so ``roughened_relief_reference_m`` is the relief both that
floor and the mobile column are measured against.  ``relief_reference_m`` records the
parent chart's own peak relief instead, because that is what the facet amplitude and the
collar taper are referenced to.  The two differ once the facets add relief, and keeping
them as separate fields is what makes the floor recomputable from the stored arrays.

Accounting keeps quarry and fill as separate ledgers that never cancel each other:
``detachment_ledger_m3`` records what the stream-power term cut,
``transport_deposition_ledger_m3`` records what the transport operator put back, and
``relaxation_transferred_ledger_m3`` records the paired internal transfers that moved
material without changing the total.  Nothing here writes back into the parent chart.
Nothing here is a certification: every status flag stays False.

## Convergence is recorded, not asserted

The repose relaxation is a finite-budget iteration: ``relax_mobile_slopes`` stops at
``max_sweeps`` and states plainly that it returns "the actual relaxed state, including an
unconverged finite-stop state".  Its own test is ``maximum_mobile_excess_after_m <=
tolerance_m``.  This module therefore stores *every operand of that test* -- per step and
in the summary (``relaxation_maximum_excess_m``, ``relaxation_tolerance_m``,
``relaxation_sweep_budget``, ``relaxation_sweeps_max``) -- and ``validate_special_form_surface``
re-derives ``relaxation_converged`` from them instead of trusting the boolean.  A bundle
may honestly record an unconverged step; it may not claim a convergence its own numbers
contradict, and a step that stops short of repose while still stalled at float64
resolution is refused outright.  The declared budgets in ``surface_preset`` were sized by
measurement (see ``DISSECTION_SOURCE``), not assumed.

1. an explicit terminal declaration for the underground reach (the engineering contract is

2. a lake-domain record for the shaft volume ``metric_natural_lakes`` expects;
3. an interior-loss contract for the closed reach, whose flux is currently hard zero.

``report.json`` (written by :func:`write_preview`) follows the shared P5 field contract so

What this module is
-------------------
Pure graph algebra over an **already assembled** receiver. It never routes terrain,
never re-derives D8, never fills a depression and never edits an edge to make a
network look complete. The channel is decided by an explicit gate mask
(``area_cells >= a_min_cells`` **or** a declared flux quantity ``>= q_min``), and the

Why it is a separate layer from ``metric_world_reaches``
-----------------------------------------------------
B2's channel rule is baked into ``resolved_mask & (receiver >= 0) & (upstream_cells >=

30 m river-network base: analytic sampling, TD detail band, seam-free mosaics.

Why this module exists
----------------------
`terrain_pipeline.hydrology_planning.coarse_condition_field` already samples the
physical conditioning field (`diffusion.geography_physical.sample_physical`) at
whatever coordinates it is handed. The river network was planned on a **10 km
page** of that field and then interpolated onto the working lattice. Two
separate things are wrong with that, and they must not be confused:

1. **Coarser than the field.** The finest structure in `sample_physical` is the
   `detail` octave `((2, 1), (1, .35))` times `geographic_scale_m = 7680 m`, i.e.
   15.36 km and **7.68 km** wavelengths. (See `geographic_noise.field`: the
   octave argument is a wavelength in grid units and `east/south` are already
   normalised by `geographic_scale_m`.)
2. **Aliased.** A 10 km page under-samples the 7.68 km octave (Nyquist for that
   octave is a 3.84 km spacing), so the page carries an *interpolation artefact*
   of that structure, not the structure itself. Measured on the reach window:
   RMS 41.88 m, max 107.43 m, i.e. 28.8% of the field standard deviation.

Sampling the same function directly at 30 m removes both, costs no GPU and no
randomness (a few microseconds per cell on CPU), and is **window-independent**:
the value at a world coordinate does not depend on which window asked for it.

So the 30 m base here is the analytic field, and Terrain Diffusion contributes a
bounded *detail band* on top of it where real sub-kilometre structure matters.
Three declared quantities, never mixed:

===============  ===================================================  ==========
quantity         what it is                                           identity
===============  ===================================================  ==========
`analytic`       `sample_physical(x, z, world_seed)` at 30 m           seed only
`td_generated`   high-frequency band of a TD window, affine-fitted    seed + model
                 onto the analytic low pass                           + window
`composed`       analytic + weight-normalised sum of detail bands      both
===============  ===================================================  ==========

Why the detail band and not the TD field
----------------------------------------
The pinned 30 m checkpoint emits elevation in **its own normalised vertical
frame**, not in world metres (`WorldPipeline._compute_elev` decodes a laplacian
pyramid; there is no metre conversion in the vendored code). On the reach window
the large scales of that output are an affine image of the analytic low pass, so
the conversion used here is a fitted line, applied **only to the band above
`detail_sigma_m`**. The band is additionally tapered to exactly zero on the
window border, which is what makes mosaics free of steps: neighbouring windows
contribute a term that is zero at the seam by construction.

What a mosaic does and does not guarantee
-----------------------------------------
Guaranteed: the large scales are the *same* analytic field everywhere, and each
window's detail term is exactly zero on that window's border, so there is no
step at a seam from the composition itself.
Not guaranteed: two windows observe independent TD samples, so their detail
bands differ where they overlap. `mosaic_detail_m` averages them by coverage
weight (`sum(w*d)/max(sum w, eps) * min(sum w, 1)`), and `seam_diagnostics`
reports the measured disagreement rather than hiding it.

Why a 10 km page must NOT be used as the "surround" of a 30 m window
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Because that is exactly where a step appears: the analytic 30 m field and the
10 km bilinear page differ by RMS 41.9 m, so a boundary between them is a
41.9 m-class cliff. The analytic field is free to evaluate anywhere, so the
30 m base is **global** and only the TD band is windowed. `transition_step_m`
quantifies this for anyone who wants to try the other way.

Lake storage from the terrain's own hypsometry, not from a vertical-wall tank.

What was wrong before
---------------------
`metric_lake_storage.LakeStorage` was already correct: it takes `cell_ids`,
`bed_elevation_m` and `cell_area_m2` and integrates the exact step function
V(h) = sum over cells of max(h - bed, 0) * area. Nothing about it assumes a
vertical wall. The vertical wall came from **the support it was given**: one
10 km planning cell, one bed value, one area. With one cell the step function
has a single step, so A(h) is 100 km2 for every stage and V(h) is a straight
line. That is a tank, and it is a property of the support, not of the class.

Measured consequence on the reach's terminal lake (`floodplain-2d-01`, and
reproduced independently here): at the declared stage the wall tank holds
4.585x the water the real basin can. The 2D run measured 4.0-4.6x.

The fix is therefore not a new lake model. It is to hand `LakeStorage` a
support whose elevation distribution is the terrain's:

* one cell per 30 m terrain cell inside the lake's own drainage depression,
* `bed_elevation_m` = the 30 m terrain height at that cell,
* `cell_area_m2` = 30 m x 30 m.

Then A(h) and V(h) are consequences of the terrain, and the cross section being
narrower lower down is just what the hypsometric curve of a real basin is. No
shape function, no exponent, no `r(x) = 1/x`, is written anywhere in this module.

How the support is derived (no tuning knobs)
--------------------------------------------
1. Priority flood from the window border (`depression_hierarchy`). The result is
the water surface a basin would settle at if it could drain off the page.
2. `fill_depth = filled - terrain`. Positive fill depth means "this cell is
   inside a depression whose exit is higher than the cell" -- measured on the
   terrain, not asserted.
3. The lake is the 4-connected component of positive fill depth containing the
   requested seed cell. Its spill level is the maximum fill level in that
   component, which *is* the height of the lowest saddle on its rim.

If the component touches the window border, the basin is not closed inside the
window and `closed_basin=False` is reported instead of silently inventing a
rim. That case is a boundary-resolution problem, not a formula problem: the
answer is a bigger window, and this module says so.

Why `max_stage_m` is the spill level
------------------------------------
A level-pool store above its spill level is not a lake any more -- it is a
flood. `LakeStorage.max_stage_m` is therefore set to the spill level, so the
class's own validation rejects a stage that would leave the basin, and
`LakeOutlet` takes over above it (that is exactly the weir law the reach solver
already uses).

What this module is
-------------------

2. splits every declared physical interval on the real 365-day calendar, so an

Scope of this module
--------------------
This is an **accounting layer**. It adds no runoff law, no delay law, no routing
kernel and no hydraulic law, and it modifies no frozen module. Everything it
reports is derived from arrays that already exist and are already validated
elsewhere:

* the soil-bucket result of
  ``terrain_pipeline.rainfall_runoff.simulate_rainfall_runoff``;
* the finite receiver graph and the per-cell reach ownership produced by
  ``terrain_pipeline.mountain_runoff_routing.build_reaches``;
* ``terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_network_accumulation.accumulate_network_discharge``
  -- the repository's one finite-graph accumulation kernel -- for the
  unknown-boundary account.

Its job is to make four things explicit and checkable that the event dictionary
previously left implicit:

1. **Where every litre goes, per cell and per physical interval.** Rain splits into
   infiltration and excess; infiltration splits into evaporation, percolation and a
   soil-store change; excess and percolation feed two linear reservoirs whose
   releases are the local river supply. Volumes are reported per cell per interval,
   and the bucket identities are *re-derived here* rather than trusted, so a bucket
   that stopped being conservative cannot pass as an accounted one.
2. **Which part of that account is an external loss and which part is an internal
   transfer.** ``percolation`` moves water from the soil store to the slow store and
   ``excess`` moves it out of the soil store into the fast store: both stay inside
   the account, so adding them to an external flux double-counts them -- the same
   mistake the reach sediment ledger already documents for
   ``eroded_loose``/``deposited``. Only evaporation leaves the bucket's accounting.
3. **That an undeclared upstream is booked as unknown and never becomes a certified
   outlet discharge.** The ``certified_*`` totals are recomputed on the cell-by-cell
   complete set only; the water withheld from them is reported as its own term, and
   the water reaching an ``unknown_boundary`` terminal is reported separately again.
   The three terms are never merged into one number.
4. **That the time-delayed routed terminal series is not re-injected as nodal
   forcing.** The nodal supply is built from the *raw* bucket release, attributed cell
   by cell, its integral is checked against that release, and the delayed terminal
   series carries an explicit ``used_for_dynamic_injection = False`` declaration at
   the call site.

Shape discipline (the defect this revision fixes)
-------------------------------------------------
``accumulate_network_discharge`` accepts exactly ``receiver.shape``, i.e. a
``[Z, X]`` block. An earlier revision of this module built ``[T, Z, X]`` blocks and
handed them straight to that kernel, so **every** call failed with
``local_q_m3_s must have matching shape and exact dtype`` and
``hydrology_ledger`` had therefore never run at all. The block builder now

``[T, Z, X]`` and ``[T, Z*X]`` remain the two accepted spellings and both are

What this module adds, and what it does not
-------------------------------------------
At TD's native 30 m a lake needs three things, and the repository already owns the
physics of each:

* **the storage curve** -- ``metric_lake_storage.LakeStorage`` integrates the exact
  step function ``V(h) = sum over cells max(h - bed, 0) * area`` over an explicit
  bed population. It is not a vertical-wall tank as long as it is handed the
  terrain's own bed population; ``metric_lake_hypsometry`` explains at length that
  the tank came from a one-cell *support*, not from the class;
* **the basin and its escape level** -- ``metric_lake_hypsometry.depression_hierarchy``
  (border-seeded priority flood) and ``depression_component``;
* **the level-pool march with saddle overflow** -- ``world_reach_lake.integrate_sill_lake``
  splits each step into storage and spill through the existing
  ``metric_lake_storage.LakeOutlet`` weir rating, capped by the water actually
  present, so its ledger closes by construction.

None of that is rewritten here. This module is the layer the repository did not
have: it **derives** the lake from a 30 m bed, **measures and checks** the lowest
saddle instead of asserting it, and **refuses** every case the window cannot
answer, with a stable reason code, before any storage is built.

The saddle trap this module is built around (measured, not argued)
------------------------------------------------------------------
"The lowest saddle is the lowest bed elevation on the basin rim" is **wrong**. On 40
noise fields (48x48, `world_seed=20261020`) the depression gate found 10 567 closed
depressions, and for **8 173** of them (77.3 %) the lowest *bed* on the 8-neighbour
rim lay **below** the level at which the basin actually escapes -- by up to
**12.54 m**. The reason is geometric, not numerical: the rim of a 4-connected
component is 8-adjacent, so it contains cells that are inside the same lake but
reachable only diagonally. Their bed is a shallow shelf, not a crossing.

What *is* provable is the flood's own answer. The priority flood assigns
``filled`` = the minimum over drainage paths to the border of the maximum elevation
on that path, so **every** cell of a closed depression carries the same ``filled``
value and that value *is* the level at which the basin escapes. Measured on the
same 40 fields plus three analytic bowls: ``max(filled) - min(filled) = 0.0`` over
the component and ``0.0`` over its rim -- exact, on all 5 301 depressions of the
second probe. So this module:

1. treats ``spill_level_m`` as ``filled`` on the basin and **verifies it is
   constant** over the basin (a measured check, not a re-derivation);
2. identifies the **exit set** -- 8-adjacent cells outside the basin whose
   ``filled`` equals that level exactly -- and requires it to be non-empty;
3. reports the naive ``min bed over rim`` separately, as a *rejected* number with
   its measured difference, so nobody can quietly adopt it again.

What it refuses, and why that is the point
------------------------------------------
A 30 m window has three ways of producing a confident and wrong lake:

1. the basin rim lies inside the untrusted border band, so the flood drained off
   the page and the reported level is the window edge, not a saddle
   (``REASON_RIM_IN_BAND``);
2. every exit cell lies inside that band, so *where* the overflow goes is
   undeclared (``REASON_SADDLE_IN_BAND``);
3. the contributing area reaches the window border, so water enters from outside
   the resolved window and neither inflow nor the storage/inflow balance can be
   judged here (``REASON_UPSTREAM_UNKNOWN``).

All three are ``truncated_not_judged``: a measurement defect, not a fact about the
terrain. The answer is a bigger window, never a smaller number reported as if it
were measured. The band is the repository's own constant
(``metric_cross_region.CONTACT_MARGIN_CELLS``), the same one the micro-depression
gate uses, so the two cannot drift apart.

Two inputs are refused for a different reason -- they are not truncation but a
wrong object:

* a **water surface is never a bed**. ``surface_kind`` is a required declaration
  and must be ``bed_elevation_m``; behaviourally, a flat or filled level field has
  zero fill depth everywhere and therefore yields ``REASON_NO_DEPRESSION`` (the
  tests feed a real lake's own filled surface back in and require the refusal);
* a **lowland that drains** (a slope, a flat, an open valley floor) has no closed
depression at the seed, so it also yields ``REASON_NO_DEPRESSION``. Being low is
  not being a lake.

A second ledger, never merged with the first
--------------------------------------------
``lake / puddle`` is a different question from ``is this basin measurable``, and
`metric_depression_gate.judge_depression` is the repository's answer to it. It is
called here on the same measured numbers and reported under ``gate``; it never
changes ``certified`` and ``certified`` never changes it. Criteria (c) growth and
(d) rim clearance are this module's own band and exit refusals, so the gate is
called with ``require_growth_convergence=False`` and every record says so.

Units, tolerances, budgets
--------------------------
elevation and stage in m, area in m2, volume in m3, physical time in s, discharge
in m3 s-1, the ``LakeOutlet`` coefficient in m3 s-1 m-1.5, spacing in m (native
30 m, cell area = spacing^2). See ``UNITS``, ``TOLERANCES`` and ``BUDGETS``; every
record carries them, so no reader has to trust this paragraph.

Above the saddle, ``LakeStorage`` cannot represent lateral flooding of the plateau
behind a sill, so the store is given ``max_stage_m = spill + head_allowance`` with
an **explicitly declared** ``head_allowance_m``. Between the two, V(h) is
``A(spill) * head`` -- a declared pondage, not measured terrain -- and the record
says so (``above_saddle_pondage_policy``). Nothing is granted silently.

One outlet-state vocabulary, and a conservative river-to-sea outlet gate.

Why this module exists
----------------------
The repository answers "where does this water end" in five disjoint vocabularies
and none of them can express *both* "interior terminal of a finite graph" and
"certified natural outlet":

* ``native_30m_source._EMITTABLE_TERMINALS`` =
  ``(inactive, interior, retained, unknown_boundary)`` -- ``open_outflow`` is
  never emitted, and ``retained`` is documented as "an interior terminal of this
  finite graph. Not a natural lake, not an outlet";
* ``metric_network_accumulation`` accepts ``open_outflow`` but never decides it;
* ``metric_depression_gate`` answers ``lake`` / ``pass_through``, with
  ``truncated_not_judged`` as a *flag*, not a verdict;
* ``metric_cross_region`` refuses with ``out_of_tile`` / ``unresolved_border`` /
  ``overlapping_disagreement`` / ``ocean`` / ``closed_basin``;
* ``natural_outlet_certification`` produces two booleans, not a graph label.

A consumer that is handed a ``retained`` terminal therefore has no honest way to
say "this is not an outlet, and here is the reason". This module is that
vocabulary plus the gate that decides when a claim may be upgraded.

The seven states, kept strictly apart
------------------------------------
``lake``                       a depression the gate judged a real water body.
``natural_outlet``             **certified** river-to-sea outlet. Only this module
                              may assign it, and only with all six evidence gates.
``retained``                   interior terminal of a finite graph. Not a lake,
                              not an outlet, not hydrologically closed.
``open_outflow``               an externally declared *open* outflow boundary:
                              water leaves here instead of ponding. The 30 m
                              source stage never emits it; declaring one is
                              evidence about a boundary, and it is the **only**
                              graph label a certification may be built on.
``unknown_boundary``           the downstream continuation left the window or met
                              unresolved support. Declared, never repaired.
``truncated_not_judged``       the depression/outlet judgement was refused because
                              the feature sat inside the untrusted border band.
``artificial_window_boundary`` a window or engineering cut. A cell on it is a
                              boundary of *this run*, not a feature of the world.

``unverified_outlet_candidate`` is deliberately **not** one of the seven: it is a
claim of ``natural_outlet`` that failed at least one gate. It exists so a failed
claim cannot be silently reported as any of the six legitimate states.

Six evidence gates, all required
-------------------------------
``continuous_downstream_coverage``
    An explicit observed path from the terminal to a coastline cell: contiguous,
    inside resolved coverage, non-increasing in bed height, endpoints exact, and
    not re-entering the terminal's own catchment. The receiver graph ends at the
    terminal (its ``receiver`` is ``-1``), so the continuation to the sea can
    only be *evidence*; requiring the receiver chain itself to reach the coast is
    what made the older raster gate refuse every multi-cell river mouth.
``not_artificial_boundary``
    The terminal's graph label is ``open_outflow``; no path cell, the coastline
    cell or the terminal lies on an artificial window edge or a declared
    engineering boundary. ``retained`` is refused unconditionally: a strictly
    downhill receiver graph says the water *stops* at a ``retained`` cell, so
    calling it a mouth would contradict the graph the certificate is built on.
    ``unknown_boundary`` is refused for the opposite reason: its continuation is
    outside this run's coverage.
``no_unknown_pollution``
    No path cell and no contributing (upstream) cell of the terminal is
    unresolved or upstream-unknown. A certified outlet must not be fed by a
    catchment whose boundary was cut. The unknown set is the caller's declared
    mask **unioned** with the set this module derives from the resolved mask (a
    resolved cell with fewer than eight resolved neighbours), so declaring an
    empty mask cannot hide a window cut.
``world_coordinate_source_pin``
    Fixed world seed, 30 m spacing, an integer native origin, every source page
    SHA256-pinned, and the declared outlet world coordinate reproducible from the
    native index lattice. No inferred coordinates.
``water_quantity_evidence``
    A finite positive discharge with named provenance and independent
    observation. A dry mouth is not an outlet.
``water_level_evidence``
    A declared vertical datum with a finite uncertainty, and a water surface at
    the outlet at or below the declared sea level *within that uncertainty*.

Failure is reported, never repaired: a refused claim keeps every reason code and
never becomes any of the six legitimate states.

Two-dimensional floodplain routing fed by a solved one-dimensional reach.

What this module is
-------------------
An **adapter layer**, not a solver. The two-dimensional shallow-water march is done
by the existing frozen local-inertial solver
(`terrain_pipeline.regional_surface_hydraulics.advance_inertial_surface`, schema
`regional-surface-local-inertial-D4-implicit-new-q-drag-v2`). This module only

* builds the D4 geometry / initial depth / boundary certificate for a window of the
  fine terrain field,
* converts a solved one-dimensional reach trace into per-cell m3/s sources, and
* closes a water ledger over the resulting two-dimensional domain.

Coupling direction (one way, 1D -> 2D)
--------------------------------------
The two-dimensional domain does **not** feed back into the reach. Water enters only
across the window boundary, at exactly the locations where a one-dimensional
`receiver` edge leaves a node inside the window and arrives at a node outside it (or
vice versa). The injected hydrograph is the saved `water_outgoing_volume_m3` of that
donor node, which is the one-dimensional solver's own account of the water it handed
across that edge. Because the injected volume is a line item the reach ledger already
removed from the donor, no cubic metre is counted twice: the two-dimensional ledger
satisfies `final = initial + injected + boundary_input - boundary_output` on its own,
and the reach ledger is left untouched.

What the terrain actually says
------------------------------
This terrain has no carved valley walls: the 10 km bilinear carrier has none of its
own, so the canonical 0.4 m carve sits on a plain tilted slope. A "bank crest"
therefore cannot be taken from the one-dimensional rectangular section (its
`depth_m` is a uniform 0.4 m carriage depth, not a terrain crest). This module derives
every crest and every outlet from the fine terrain it is given, and refuses to invent
one where the terrain does not supply it.

Full-grid (canonical PL mesh) dynamic bed coupling for the finite world reach.

Why this module exists
----------------------
`world_channel_dynamics.couple_nodal_reach` advances only the **nodal** bed: the
canonical carved PL mesh saved by `build_channel_geometry` is never updated
(`dynamic_geometry_mode = nodal_bed_only_initial_PL_mesh_not_updated`), so every
map of the bed still shows the initial carve.

The canonical mesh coupling `metric_morphology_coupling.couple_morphology` *does*
update the mesh, but it refuses this reach at

    if np.any(areas < network.width_m * network.length_m - 1e-9):
        raise ValueError("material basis area below hydraulic control area")

(`metric_morphology_coupling.py:300-301`). That guard is **not relaxed** here and
the threshold is unchanged; this module only replaces the *mapping* from node
volume to mesh vertices, and it demonstrates that the old mapping was the thing
that could not pass.

Why the old mapping cannot pass (measured, not argued)
-----------------------------------------------------
The old `_basis` gives every vertex to its nearest centreline node, over the
carved vertices only (`cut_depth_m > 1e-10`), and the material area is the exact
piecewise-linear integral `A_i = sum_t A_t * mean_k(basis_i)`. Because
`sum_k win_k(t) == 1` on every triangle, the **supremum over every possible
vertex partition** of the carved vertices is reached exactly when all three
corners of every triangle are owned, i.e.

    supremum = sum_t A_t * frac_carved(t) = 7.0928e8 m^2

while the hydraulic control demand is `sum_i W_i L_i = 7.5727e8 m^2`. The
supremum is below the demand by 6.34%, so **no partition of the carved vertices
satisfies the guard** -- not nearest-node, not ribbon, not width-weighted, not
any fractional unit partition. The shortfall is exactly the mass-lumping leak of
the boundary triangles: a triangle that touches the carved corridor but has
corners outside it can only ever contribute its carved corners' share.

The guard is about one thing: a node's deposition volume must not be squeezed
into less mesh than the water body it was computed for. The correct fix is to
close the support so the partition is *complete*: take the carved vertices plus
the ring of vertices belonging to any triangle that touches a carved vertex.
That ring supplies 8.4997e8 m^2 (1.1224x the demand) and the guard passes with
nothing about it changed.

The mapping
-----------
l) support = carved vertices closed under triangle incidence (one 50 m ring);
2) every control node owns the three vertices of one triangle containing it, so
the basis is **cardinal** at every node (`_sample_nodes` reproduces the node
change exactly) -- this is what makes "the mesh moved but the node did not"
impossible;
3) the remaining support vertices are handed out by a deterministic,
area-targeted fill: each free vertex goes to the reachable node with the largest
remaining deficit per metre, so every node's material area meets or exceeds its
`W_i * L_i` control area;
4) per interval, the Exner delta is scattered onto the mesh, the node bed is
re-sampled **from the updated mesh**, and the slope and hydraulic section are
rebuilt before the next macro step. The next macro step therefore solves water
on the changed bed.

What is reused unchanged
------------------------
`solve_sediment` (old replay/Exner inventory), `solve_channel` (old Manning finite
volume), `make_channel_product`, `receiver_distances`, `bed_from_inventory` (which
already divides by `1 - porosity`; nothing here divides twice). No transport law,
no roughness and no geometry algorithm is re-derived.

Ledger
------
Mobile sand, loose bed sand, cumulative rock erosion, cumulative deposition,
cumulative loose erosion, cumulative export and the initial carve are recorded
**separately**, and their aggregates carry an explicit numeric residual.

Scope of this module (phase 1, user-approved simplification)
-----------------------------------------------------------

calibrated property of any field site** (``PROVENANCE``). Mohs hardness and

Conservative bedrock -> regolith -> parent-material inventory with mass closure.

Scope (G9 minimum, one thing only)
---------------------------------
A finite column of weatherable bedrock is attacked for a declared time step. The
products are tracked as separate accounts and must close exactly:

    bedrock solid removed = regolith solid produced + dissolved solid exported

Nothing here invents parent material. ``parent_solid_m3`` is a **view** of part of
the regolith solid (the fine fraction declared for soil supply), not a new store.
Pore conversion (solid -> bulk) happens exactly once, at production.

Drivers
-------
Weathering depth rate is a declared product of the available conditions:

    physical  = k_physical * (1 - bed_hardness)
    chemical  = k_chemical * solubility * moisture * temperature_factor
    biogenic  = k_biological * bio_activity * moisture * temperature_factor
    depth_rate = (physical + chemical + biogenic) * dt_s

temperature_factor = Q10 ** ((T - T_ref) / 10). A **negative** temperature is a
legal input and simply gives a smaller factor; it is never treated as invalid.
All coefficient names, units, provenance and value statuses are declared, and the
result records them so a reader can see this is an engineering reference set, not
a global calibration.

The rate is **hard-capped** by the remaining weatherable thickness in every step,
so the stock can be exhausted but never overdrawn.

Not here
--------
* no soil-water bucket, no ET, no groundwater, no vegetation growth model;
* no transport to the river or to the sea: the two supply functions only report
  what is *available*, they do not move it;
* no default-world wiring, no file IO, no hashing, no unrequested defensive layers.

A3 acceptance: a declared unknown upstream spreads everywhere downstream and nowhere else.

Fixture
-------
One 15x15 pure-synthetic window (no saved page, no generation): a descending ring
ramp that leaves the window through one ``unknown_boundary`` cut, plus two
independent strict-downhill cones with two ``retained`` interior terminals. The
cones give the graph what a degenerate single chain cannot: confluences of up to
eight donors, a real divide between two branches, and -- once a hole is dug -- a
non-empty contaminated set *plus* a disjoint, untouched branch.

Three windows are built by the production entry ``build_strict_topology``:

``clean``      every cell resolved;
``headwater``  one interior cell unresolved, and *no* resolved cell drains into it;
``donor``      one interior cell unresolved that three resolved cells dropped into.

The second and third are what A3 asks for: a ``valid_mask=False`` hole dug in the
middle of an otherwise known graph.

Independence of every expected answer
-------------------------------------
No expectation in this file is computed with the code under test. The expected
incompleteness comes from three independent steps: (1) the unknown seeds are
derived from the validity mask by an eight-neighbour count written here, (2) each
seed's downstream cone is obtained by walking the production receiver **forward**
one cell at a time, and (3) each cell's own catchment is obtained by walking it
**backward** through a donor map built here. ``accumulate_network_discharge`` and
the private ``_complete`` helper of ``tools.native_30m_query`` are deliberately
not imported: reusing them would let a single direction bug agree with itself.
The gates are exercised only as black boxes through ``require_available``,
``query_point``, ``census`` and the diagnostic product's own gate.

Closing the hole legally, instead of feeding an illegal graph
-------------------------------------------------------------
Digging a hole makes the *previous* receiver of that cell stale. This file never
hands such a graph to production and then calls the outcome an unknown-propagation
bug. Instead, every window is rebuilt from its own validity mask, so what reaches
production is the legal strict-D8 graph of that window. ``test_hole_is_closed_
legally_and_never_reached_by_a_receiver`` additionally proves the closure is
explicit: no receiver of a resolved cell is the hole, the hole's former donors
are re-targeted onto resolved cells (the changed set is exactly the hole plus
those donors), and the illegal clean-receiver/holed-mask combination is refused
outright by the production builder -- so "the hole is a hole" can never be
reported as "unknown propagated wrongly". The hole's unknown inflow is declared
through the very ``upstream_unknown_mask`` array the topology stage emits; the
zero stored at the hole in ``local_q_m3_s`` is the storage convention for a
non-participating cell, not a claim that no water entered.

Q is a synthetic field of exact multiples of 1/8, so every catchment sum is exact
in float64 and "bit-identical" below is a real statement, not a tolerance.

What this file does not claim
-----------------------------
That the strict-D8 kernel itself is right (other tests own that), that the
diagnostic product authenticates its inputs, or that any number here is
hydraulically usable: ``hydraulic_ready`` and ``publishable`` stay false.

Independent cold-read audit of a prepared river-backbone product.

What this tool is
-----------------
A **separate process** that reads a product directory and re-derives every published number
with its own implementation. It imports nothing from the producer: no
``metric_backbone_precompute``, no ``metric_network_accumulation``, no
``metric_domain_closure``, no ``native_30m_source``. The import ban is asserted at start-up
by scanning ``sys.modules``, so a transitive import cannot slip in.

What it checks
--------------
1. the product's bytes, headers, budget and identity (through the shared read-only codec);
2. an **independent per-cell walk**: reach chains, coverage, anchors, handoff and terminal
   edges, upstream areas, the area's completeness, every quantity's routed field and that
   quantity's own completeness;
3. the declared side inputs, re-solved independently: one chosen source per branch, its
   delivery compared, and the deliberate double count shown to be detectable;
4. with ``--reference-rows``: the A-gate edge, anchor and split-relation check;
5. with ``--compare-product``: the cross-window acceptance.

There is no "verify accumulation on load" switch: a product stores only its parent's
identity, which cannot re-derive the parent's topology, and re-running the network on every
read is exactly what this design refuses. The full rebuild is the producer's own
``validate_backbone`` before publishing; this audit is the independent second opinion.

Cross-window acceptance, correctly stated
-----------------------------------------
"Strictly interior" only means the cell has a complete 8-neighbourhood; it does **not** mean
its upstream is closed. The same world cell can therefore carry a different upstream member
set, a different area and a different routed flux in two windows. So a value is compared
only where **all** of these hold, separately per quantity:

* the cell is strictly interior in **both** windows;
* that quantity's own completeness is ``True`` on both sides;
* the **world upstream member set is equal**, computed here by an independent reverse walk
  (not read off ``complete_mask``);
* the quantity's input exists (status ``available``) and both sides declare the same input
  provenance digest.

Every other cell is listed with a reason; nothing is dropped and no completeness is inferred
from the area's. ``receiver`` is compared in **world** coordinates, because a flat index
carries the column count of its own window.

A reach id is only required to be equal when the whole ordered path lies strictly interior
*and* every node of it is complete on both sides; a boundary-crossing or partially pending
reach is reported as ``not_comparable_context``. Because an OR gate may legitimately **split**
an A-only reach, this audit does not require the OR segmentation to be an ordered
subsequence of the B2 segments. It requires what actually matters: every A-gate directed
edge of the reference network appears in the OR edge set, every confluence anchor and reach
endpoint is preserved or is a declared split point, and the split/merge relation is written
out per reach.

Read-only on-demand river consistency auditor.

This is the referee for the infinite-world river work: it measures whether an
arbitrary world coordinate can be planned at all, and whether the products two
overlapping windows produce for the same world coordinates agree.

It generates nothing that is published, certifies nothing and writes no
verification evidence. It only counts and compares.

What it checks
--------------
1. acceptance  - how many macro cells plan successfully, and every rejection
                 reason (verbatim, so a new reason can never hide as "other")
2. determinism - the same cell planned twice must give one identity
3. cross-window agreement on the physical overlap between neighbouring cells,
   split into: shared base condition, published height, flow direction,
   river mask, and PHYSICAL OUTLET ownership (which outlet world point a cell
   drains to). Outlet is used on purpose, not the owner_domain_id integer:
   `general` mode numbers domains by `enumerate(sorted(selected_terminals))`,
   so the same physical domain gets a different integer in every window and
   comparing those integers over-counts disagreement (pure label noise -- it
   once reported 2533 "owner disagreements" that mean nothing)
4. load order - the same set of cells planned in shuffled order must give the
   same products

Axis note (this bit us once already): support arrays are (z-rows, x-columns)
and adjacent cells are 320 km apart while a support is 1280 km wide, so two
neighbours share 3/4 of a support. A cell differing in z shifts ROWS; a cell
differing in x shifts COLUMNS. Comparing along the wrong axis produces absurd
numbers (it once reported the shared base condition differing by 4635 m, which
cannot happen because that field is a pure function of world coordinates).

Embed Terrain Diffusion detail into one saved coarse reach window.

Why
---
The cross-region reach runs (`tools/run_full_reach*.py`) solve on the 10 km
coarse world. Their near-field terrain is therefore the **bilinear
interpolation** of a 10 km grid, which looks smooth next to any real landscape.
This tool produces a declared 30 m terrain page for one 15.39 km window that

* carries real Terrain Diffusion (TD) detail for the fine texture,
* keeps the *large scales* equal to the solved coarse field, and
* keeps the canonical carved channel exactly where the solver put it, so the
  river still sits in the valley floor instead of floating over it.

What is generated and what is not
---------------------------------
1. **TD generated** - one native window of the pinned 30 m checkpoint
   (`models/terrain-diffusion-30m`) run through the repository's own
   `diffusion.physical_backend.PhysicalTerrainDiffusionBackend` (which refuses
   to run without CUDA; no guard is bypassed here).
2. **Interpolated** - the coarse 10 km page bilinearly sampled onto the fine
   lattice, and the TD field's long wavelengths, which are **removed** by a
   low pass so that the fine page cannot drift away from the solved world.
3. **Carved** - the canonical carved bed of the saved geometry, re-expressed on
   the fine lattice as a cut depth. Inside the carved footprint the field is
   the solved bed; TD detail is damped to zero there and ramps back in outside
   it, so there is no floating channel and no ridge across the trench.

No random source other than the fixed world seed is used: the TD pipeline seed
is the world seed itself (it drives both the conditioning field and the latent
noise). A derived `td-detail` sub-seed is recorded for provenance, but it is
NOT used, because changing the conditioning seed would change the world the
coarse solve belongs to (verified numerically; see the alignment diagnostics).

Phase-wise sediment budget over fixed reference-defined delta regions.

The public function :func:`summarize_phase_regions` summarizes per-phase bed
change (bulk volumes, m^3) against regions fixed on a reference bed and,
separately, the endpoint budget implied by ``final_bed_m - reference_bed_m``.

Regions (all overlapping diagnostics, NOT independent ledger partitions):
  * ``region_all_ocean``     - every valid ocean cell.
  * ``region_near_sea_level``- valid ocean cells with |reference - sea_level| <= band_m.
  * ``region_above_sea_level``- valid ocean cells with reference > sea_level.

Reported JSON keys and meanings:
  * ``spacing_m``: cell size (m); cell area is ``spacing_m**2``.
  * ``sea_level_m``, ``band_m``: region definitions as passed in.
  * ``phase_names``: unique phase names in first-seen order.
  * ``cell_area_m2``: ``spacing_m**2``.
  * ``regions``: dict keyed by region name, each with
      - ``cell_count``: number of cells in the region.
      - ``area_m2``: ``cell_count * cell_area_m2``.
      - ``phase_net_m3``: per unique phase, sum of delta over region (m^3).
      - ``phase_positive_m3``: per phase, sum of positive deltas (>=0, m^3).
      - ``phase_negative_m3``: per phase, sum of negative deltas (<=0, m^3).
      - ``phase_net_total_m3``: sum over phases of phase_net_m3 (m^3).
      - ``endpoint_m3``: sum over region of (final-reference)*cell_area (m^3).
      - ``residual_m3``: ``endpoint_m3 - phase_net_total_m3`` (signed, preserved).
  * ``reference_area_m2``/``n_phases`` top-level keys are intentionally omitted.

Per-phase positive/negative bed-change volumes are NOT gross particle sediment
deposition/erosion: they are sign-split sums of the bulk bed change. Regions
overlap and must not be summed as independent partitions.

Inputs are not mutated. Invalid cells (where ``valid_mask`` is False) may hold
NaN and are excluded from finiteness checks and from all statistics. Finite
arrays are validated explicitly on ALL valid cells.

Prepare one river-backbone product from declared inputs, then audit it cold.

This tool is **scheduling and I/O only**. The gates, the segmentation, the per-quantity
completeness and the side-input contracts belong to
``terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_backbone_precompute``; the product format belongs
to ``terrain_pipeline.surface_rivers.metric_backbone_product``. Nothing algorithmic lives

Flow, in this order and no other
--------------------------------
1. the support is **declared before any page is read**: world seed, 30 m spacing, signed
   native origin, ``shape_zx``, the plan version and the cell budget;
2. the pinned TD pages are read through ``native_30m_source.load_native_window`` with their
   SHA256 pins, so real pages are read and hashed rather than trusted;
3. the B1 parent is rebuilt through ``metric_world_domains.domain_candidates`` and its
   identity must equal the pinned evidence identity -- a rebuild that drifts is refused
   before any backbone exists;
4. the flux quantities are loaded from **explicit** inputs only (a declared event model or
   a declared climatology estimate); there is no built-in climate estimator, and a missing
   input becomes ``not_available_pending`` rather than zero;
5. the backbone is built and written into a hidden partial directory;
6. a **separate process** runs ``tools/audit_river_backbone.py`` against that partial
   directory;
7. only a PASS is renamed into the requested output path. A failure keeps the partial
   evidence under a ``*.rejected*`` name and the output path stays absent, so a failing run
   can never leave something that looks like a product.

End-to-end L0 special-terrain preview on a real pinned Terrain Diffusion 1 m bed.

This tool runs the thin adapter over the pinned 30 m hierarchy and the shared fine bed:

    pinned hierarchy -> selected fine window -> chart -> L0 field form -> preview

The identity chain of every produced bundle is recorded so the form geometry can be traced
back to the exact fine bed, native window and source hierarchy. Everything it writes lands
in a scratch evidence directory: never a source cache, never ``verification/``. Two cases
run end to end, because the shared fine bed is capped at 240x240 cells:

* a full-size ``volcanic_plug`` preset on the coarsest allowed bed (4 m, 960 m window);
* a single-centre ``karst_tower_field`` tower on the true 1 m bed (240 m window).

The second case is the closest this revision gets to a real-metre landform: the targets are
placed at the window centre by the caller. That placement is a declared assumption, not a
claim about where such a tower exists.

The field-form module fills terrain up to a declared *absolute* surface and never excavates
(``displacement = max(relief - bed, 0)``). A preset whose ``base_elevation_m`` is 0 m would
therefore sit about 1.4 km below the pinned bed and produce exactly zero relief - a silent,
all-zero form. This tool declares the foot elevation of every target as the minimum bed
elevation over the selected window and records that basis per case, so the declaration is
visible instead of implied. It is an assumption of the caller, not a surveyed value, and it
is the reason the two cases here are *fills against a real bed*, not reconstructions.

What this does
--------------
Takes the finished one-dimensional reach of `full-reach-run-02` and drives a
two-dimensional local-inertial march (the frozen
`regional-surface-local-inertial-D4-implicit-new-q-drag-v2` solver, unchanged) over a

donor node's own saved `water_outgoing_volume_m3`. Nothing flows back. Every injected
cubic metre is a line item the reach ledger already removed from the donor, so the
two-dimensional ledger closes on its own and no volume is counted twice.

Labels used throughout (they are kept apart on purpose):

* **marginal edge** -- a distribution measured on **one grid** for **one axis**: the
  landform ordinals on the published ``literal_metre`` artifact, and the climate
  variants on a grid covering a full latitude period.
* **co-located joint observation** -- on **one and the same grid**, how many of the
  16 ``(ordinal, variant)`` slots actually occur together.  That is what a world
  can show inside a single window; it is reported for the published 15.27 km
  window and for a large grid spanning one latitude period.
* **direct-product reachability** -- ``{(ordinal, variant)}`` of the two measured
  marginal edges, mapped through ``palette_index`` to the 16 frozen palette names.
  This says the 16 slots are *addressable*, **not** that 16 slots were observed on
  one grid.

The acceptance grid is 12 columns x 96 rows over x 0..880 km and z 0..one whole
latitude period (1 920 km), which is §7.1's ">= 1 complete latitude period".  The contract's
§6.1 probe lattice (1 900 km = 0.99 periods, deliberately stopping short of the seam) is
re-run only to reproduce that probe's published share table, and the period-coverage claim
is kept on the 1 920 km grid alone.  A denser 24 x 192 cross-check grid, a five-phase
robustness sweep of the z origin, and a precipitation-saturation lattice sweep are run as
well.

The two axes move on different scales (contract §6.3, measured): the landform
ordinal ``dominant_type`` changes within ~15 km of terrain while the climate
``variant`` needs one full ``LATITUDE_PERIOD_M`` (1 920 km) to walk a period.  On
the published 15.27 km window the ordinal edge shows all four values and the
climate edge shows **one** value.  That is a sample fact about that window and
seed; this script makes **no** universal claim that no window anywhere can hold

Read-only special-terrain surface bundles for the local review UI.

A chart in this package is a *synthetic analytic* landform study, not a georeferenced
landscape: the four bundles are pinned by a manifest that carries each archive's digest
and identity, and the reader refuses to touch a file whose digest or identity has moved.
Nothing here advances physics, writes a routing graph or certifies a channel -- the four
capability flags stay false, and the display is an illustration of stored arrays.

The manifest is pinned by its own SHA256 as well, so a *metadata* edit to a bundle entry
cannot quietly re-point a case at a different archive: adding a form means re-pinning the
manifest constant, which is a deliberate source change rather than a silent one.  This is
the same shape as ``saved_surface.ACCEPTANCE_SHA``, one level down.

Mesh arrays are shipped as one JSON descriptor plus separate binary bodies, following
``saved_surface``: the vertex blob is the stored ``vertices_xyz_m`` minus its own AABB
minimum, and the triangle index blob is the stored ``triangles``.  Topology is therefore
*reused*, never rebuilt, and the frontend can hand both straight to ``THREE.BufferAttribute``.
